ev.q: During 2001, an estimated 935,556 men and 1,731,640 women aged > 65 years were treated in EDs for nonfatal injuries.
The overall injury rate per 100,000 persons was higher among women (8,466 per 100,000 persons) than among men (6,404).

The majority (82%) of older adults were treated and released; 16% were hospitalized.
Overall, falls resulted in the highest rates of injury (4,684 per 100,000 persons)
The injury rate from falls was higher among women (5,659) than men (3,319).
CDC analyzed data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System-All Injury Program

methods_quotes.q: Data from these cases are weighted by the inverse of the probability of selection to produce national estimates
A direct variance estimation procedure was used to calculate 95% confidence intervals and to account for the complex sample design
U.S. Census Bureau population estimates for 2001 were used to calculate injury rates
Injuries of unknown intent were grouped with those classified as unintentional.
